craft_notes: Sthāyin: taste-honor (six tastes). Rows: row 3 (feasts→honor). Close: honor (namāmi refrain for the outer petals). Rejected: 'flavors' — killed: tastes kept (rasa as taste, doctrinal); 'lives/dwells' for abiding — killed: abiding kept (nilayā as shrine-dwelling).

lines: On wealth-lord's sprout abiding, who with varied six-taste feasts —
honors Bhairava ever, tongue-called Cāmuṇḍā — honor.
l4.sanskrit_cite: dhanapatikisalayanilayā yā nityaṃ vividhaṣaḍrasāhāraiḥ | pūjayati bhairavaṃ tāṃ jihvābhikhyāṃ namāmi cāmuṇḍām

reads_against.argmap: Who offers taste? → Cāmuṇḍā (jihvā/tongue, Kubera/north petal) offers the six tastes.
c1_essence: Cāmuṇḍā tongue-called honors with six-taste foods from the north: tasting itself offered.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder circling home to rest)
